moderately.definition: to certain extent or degree; "pretty big"; "pretty bad"; "jolly decent of him"; "the shoes are priced reasonably"; "he is fairly clever with computers"

modestly.definition: with modesty; in a modest manner; "the dissertation was entitled, modestly, `Remarks about a play by Shakespeare'"

modishly.definition: in a stylish manner; "He was smartly dressed"

moistly.definition: in a damp manner; "a scarf was tied round her head but the rebellious curl had escaped and hung damply over her left eye"

momentarily.definition: for an instant or moment; "we paused momentarily before proceeding"; "a cardinal perched momently on the dogwood branch"

momently.definition: for an instant or moment; "we paused momentarily before proceeding"; "a cardinal perched momently on the dogwood branch"

monaurally.definition: in a monaural manner; "the stimuli were presented monaurally"

monolingually.definition: in a monolingual manner; "she had been reared monolingually"

monotonously.definition: in a monotonous manner; "the history of the play throughout the latter part of the eighteenth century is monotonously uneventful"

monstrously.definition: in a hideous manner; "her face was hideously disfigured after the accident"

moodily.definition: in a moody manner; "in the bar, a youngish, sharp-eyed man was staring moodily into a gin and tonic"

moonily.definition: in a dreamy manner; "`She would look beautiful in the new dress,' Tommy said dreamily"

morally.definition: with respect to moral principles; "morally unjustified"

morbidly.definition: in a morbid manner or to a morbid degree; "he was morbidly fascinated by dead bodies"

mordaciously.definition: in a mordacious manner; "she taunted him mordaciously"

moreover.definition: in addition; "computer chess games are getting cheaper all the time; furthermore, their quality is improving"; "the cellar was dark; moreover, mice nested there"; "what is more, there's no sign of a change"

morosely.definition: in a morose manner; "he fell morosely on the bed"

morphologically.definition: in a morphological manner; with regard to morphology; "these two plants are morphologically related"

mortally.definition: in such a manner that death ensues (also in reference to hatred, jealousy, fear, etc.); "a being of whom the forest Indians are said to be mortally afraid, with a hoof shaped like the heel of a bottle"

mostly.definition: in large part; mainly or chiefly; "These accounts are largely inactive"

motionlessly.definition: without moving; in a motionless manner; "he saw the black-haired man waiting motionlessly behind the opposite side of the platform"

mournfully.definition: in a mournful manner; "the young man stared into his glass mournfully"

movingly.definition: in a moving manner; "she sang movingly"

mulishly.definition: in a stubborn unregenerate manner; "she remained stubbornly in the same position"

multifariously.definition: in diverse ways; "the alternatives that are variously represented by the participants"; "the speakers treated the subject most diversely"

multilaterally.definition: in a multilateral manner;so as to affect many parties or governments; "they worked out an agreement unilaterally"

multiplicatively.definition: in a multiplicative manner; "the errors increased multiplicatively"

munificently.definition: in a generous manner; "he gave liberally to several charities"

murderously.definition: as if bent on murder; "the huge dog bore down on them with bared fangs and barking murderously"

musically.definition: in a musical manner; "She sang very musically"

musingly.definition: in a reflective manner; "`It's funny about that bar,' he said musingly"

mutely.definition: without speaking; "he sat mutely next to her"

mutually.definition: in a mutual or shared manner; "the agreement was mutually satisfactory"; "the goals of the negotiators were not reciprocally exclusive"

mysteriously.definition: in a cryptic manner; "`we will meet again', he said cryptically"
